instructions: Cut the brisket into 2-inch chunks, trimming off any thick pieces of hard fat. Peel the potatoes and cut them into large chunks. Chop 2 of the tomatoes small and cut the third into big wedges. Cut the green onions into 2-inch lengths and slice the ginger.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large heavy pot over high heat. Add the green onions and ginger and stir for 30 seconds. Add the brisket, sprinkle it with 1/2 tsp salt and stir for 3 minutes, until the fat starts to melt and the edges are browned. Move the brisket to a bowl.
Turn the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp oil and the chopped tomatoes. Cook for 4 minutes, until they fall apart into a sauce. Put the brisket back in and stir for 1 minute.

Turn the heat to high. Add 2 1/2 cups hot water, the star anise, cinnamon stick, 2 tsp sugar, 3 tbsp oyster sauce, 4 tsp light soy sauce, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the tomato wedges. Bring to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and simmer for 1 hour 15 minutes, stirring now and then.

While the stew simmers, rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a pot with 2 1/4 cups water, bring to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Leave it covered for 10 minutes.
Add the potatoes to the stew, cover and simmer for 20 minutes, until the brisket is tender enough to pull apart with a fork and the potatoes are soft in the middle.

Take out the star anise and cinnamon stick. Turn the heat to high and boil, uncovered, for 5 minutes, until the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Spoon the stew over the rice and serve.
Let leftovers cool, then keep them covered in the fridge for up to 4 days or freeze them for up to 3 months. Reheat in a pot over low heat with a splash of water, stirring now and then.
method_notes: Every version agrees on the same shape: brisket browned with green onion and ginger, tomatoes cooked into a sauce, star anise and cinnamon in the pot, potatoes added near the end. The Cantonese Cook (the only version with a rating, 5 from one vote) is the lead for the ingredients and ratios, scaled from 6 servings to 4. Its 25 minute simmer is too short for brisket, so the braise time comes from Woks of Love and Yun's Family Table, which both simmer for 1 to 1 1/2 hours. The sources are thinly rated, so this is a fallback lead. It makes a big pot that keeps.
